tema: Evaluates the efficacy of repeating immunoadsorption (IA) in ME/CFS patients who had previously responded.
diseno: Open pilot study in 5 ME/CFS patients retreated about two years later with a modified IA protocol; 12-month follow-up with specific scales and anti-β2AR antibodies by ELISA.
hallazgos: An 80-90% decrease in total IgG and anti-β2AR antibodies was achieved; IA was well tolerated. Four patients improved rapidly in several symptoms for 6-12 months and one did not improve.
conclusion: IA shows clinical efficacy in ME/CFS and justifies controlled studies; it could be integrated as initial therapy in patients with autoantibodies to achieve rapid relief.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent on the autoimmune hypothesis and the efficacy of IA. The PDF conclusions are somewhat more assertive ('IA is effective') than a sample of 5 patients without a control allows, a nuance that the abstract does acknowledge by calling for controlled trials.

tema: Describes three CFS cases with a neuromuscular transmission defect and cholinergic dysautonomia that responded to low-dose pyridostigmine.
diseno: Series of 3 cases (women aged 18, 28 and 29) evaluated with repetitive nerve stimulation, CASS scale and EBV serology; treatment with oral pyridostigmine (10-30 mg).
hallazgos: All three patients showed an incremental response of 42-60% to repetitive stimulation, mild cholinergic involvement and positive anti-VCA IgG antibodies against EBV; all improved with pyridostigmine.
conclusion: It is proposed that the fatigue of some patients could be due to a mild neuromuscular transmission defect with cholinergic dysautonomia, perhaps through cross-reactivity of antibodies against EBV with calcium channels; the authors acknowledge that the sample is too small.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and discussion are consistent on pyridostigmine and neuromuscular transmission. The discussion adds the mechanistic hypothesis about EBV, absent from the keywords, and is more cautious about definitive conclusions.

tema: To evaluate the efficacy of faecal microbiota transplantation on fatigue and quality of life in CFS.
diseno: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot trial: 11 patients, universal donor FMT (n=5) versus autologous FMT (n=6) by colonoscopy; VAS, MFIS, 15D and EQ-5D-3L at 1 and 6 months.
hallazgos: No significant differences in VAS or MFIS at 1 and 6 months; 15D and EQ-5D-3L did not change; no adverse events.
conclusion: FMT was safe but did not relieve symptoms or improve quality of life; the small sample limits generalization.
triangulacion: Full coherence among the three sources; it contrasts with the earlier, more favourable retrospective FMT study.

tema: Compares ventricular lactate levels in CFS, fibromyalgia (FM), both and controls to evaluate the unitary hypothesis.
diseno: Comparative neuroimaging study with proton magnetic resonance spectroscopy (1H MRSI), normalized data from two studies; sample size not stated.
hallazgos: Ventricular CSF lactate did not differ between CFS, FM and CFS+FM, but was significantly higher in the three groups than in controls.
conclusion: Ventricular lactate distinguishes patients from controls, but is not a viable biomarker to differentiate CFS from FM or from overlapping cases.
triangulacion: The conclusions come from the abstract, so they agree fully with it; the keywords (heterogeneity, biomarkers, overlap) are consistent. Paradoxically, the stated aim was to support distinct processes and the result does not achieve it.

tema: Investigates endothelial dysfunction and endothelial biomarkers in patients with post-COVID syndrome, including those meeting ME/CFS criteria.
diseno: Case-control study: 30 patients with post-COVID syndrome (14 with ME/CFS) and 15 matched seronegative controls; reactive hyperaemia index (RHI) by peripheral arterial tonometry; in a larger cohort with convalescents, ET-1, Ang-2, endocan, IL-8, ACE and ACE2.
hallazgos: Five of 14 patients with post-COVID ME/CFS and five of 16 with post-COVID syndrome showed decreased RHI (< 1.67), versus no controls. ET-1 was elevated in both groups and Ang-2 was lower in post-COVID and convalescents; RHI correlated paradoxically with age, pressure and BMI only in post-COVID.
conclusion: A subgroup of post-COVID patients shows peripheral endothelial dysfunction and altered biomarkers, with profiles that could indicate different mechanisms between subgroups.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions are consistent; the PDF conclusions note as a limitation the absence of convalescents in the RHI assessment (followed by table noise).

tema: Explores how the initial level of available energy modulates the relationship between staying within the energy envelope and functioning in ME and CFS.
diseno: Comparative study of six groups according to available energy (high or low) and adherence to the energy envelope (under-extended, within, over-extended); pooled data from several centres; size not stated.
hallazgos: Those with more available energy functioned better, but this relationship was less marked in those who overexerted themselves.
conclusion: The results support the energy envelope theory and suggest that overexertion affects especially those with more available energy.
triangulacion: Keywords (overexertion, activity) and abstract are consistent. The conclusions (discussion) are limited to limitations: self-reported data, lack of diversity and need for longitudinal and experimental designs.

tema: Reviews the interactions between environmental, neuroimmune and nitro-oxidative stress factors in the pathophysiology of CFS.
diseno: Narrative literature review on immune alterations, environmental factors, infections and nutritional deficits.
hallazgos: The most frequent immune alterations are changes in immunoglobulins, B and T lymphocyte phenotypes and cytokine profiles, and lower NK cell cytotoxicity; some markers (activation, PKR activity) have moderate diagnostic performance. The activated nitro-oxidative pathways would explain key symptoms; infections, low-dose radiation, metals and selenium deficiency would aggravate the picture.
conclusion: Complex interactions between immune and nitro-oxidative pathways, infectious agents, environmental factors and nutritional deficits contribute to the pathophysiology of CFS; antioxidants and lipid replacement could have some efficacy.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent on immune dysfunction, NK, PKR and oxidative stress. The PDF conclusions broaden this with mitochondrial dysfunction, specific biomarkers (isoprostanes, TRPM3) and exposure to radiation or metals.

tema: Systematically reviews the epigenetic data on ME/CFS to look for common pathways and explore possible activation of transposable elements.
diseno: PRISMA systematic review of DNA methylation and non-coding RNA studies in ME/CFS, with screening for transposable elements using Dfam, Repbase and RepeatMasker. The earlier studies totalled 230 patients and 115 controls in methylation, and 127 and 128 in non-coding RNA.
hallazgos: Unexpected associations were found between transposable elements and the epigenetic marks of ME/CFS. A model emerges in which transcriptional induction of latent transposons would activate innate immunity without active infection.
conclusion: Transcriptomic analyses should not filter out repetitive sequences and broad epigenetic databases and targeted assays are needed to confirm or rule out the involvement of transposons.
triangulacion: The three sources agree on epigenetics, transposons and non-coding RNA. The conclusions stress the scarcity and heterogeneity of the studies and propose hypomethylation as the mechanism, with a more hypothetical tone.

tema: Reviews the immunopathobiology of Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) and proposes that latently infected cells that escape immune surveillance could give rise to ME/CFS in a subgroup of patients.
diseno: Review with hypothesis formulation based on the literature on the pathogenesis of ME/CFS, autoimmune diseases and cancers associated with EBV.
hallazgos: Alterations of cellular immunity, increased Th2 response, expanded EBV-infected cells and elevated anti-EBV antibodies are described. A subgroup with HLA DRB1 and DQB1 alleles that would confer greater susceptibility to EBV and immunodeficiency through immune evasion is postulated.
conclusion: They propose investigating whether anti-EBV therapies (including demethylating agents and adoptive immunotherapy with specific T lymphocytes) would be effective in selected patients, and studying people with post-mononucleosis fatigue.
triangulacion: Keywords (EBV latency, immune evasion, T lymphocyte surveillance), abstract and discussion are consistent. The discussion provides the therapeutic model of the figure and a lot of noise (funding, acknowledgements); the authors acknowledge that the evidence is inconclusive.

tema: Proposes that latency and recurrent reactivation of EBV generate an acquired immunodeficiency common to ME/CFS and long COVID.
diseno: Hypothesis article based on a literature review; provides no own data.
hallazgos: Both conditions share immune alterations, viral persistence, autoimmunity, chronic inflammation, hypocortisolism, microclots and EBV reactivation. A three-step model is proposed: acquired immunodeficiency in carriers of 'weak' HLA-II haplotypes, ectopic lymphoid structures with EBV latency (including the CNS) and immune exhaustion.
conclusion: In long COVID, prior SARS-CoV-2 infection in individuals with weak HLA-II haplotypes would precede this process; the discussion also links the kynurenine pathway, serotonin and nitrosative stress with fatigue and viral latency.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract are consistent on EBV, long COVID and acquired immunodeficiency. The discussion fragment focuses on serotonergic and kynurenine mechanisms not announced in the keywords, and contains administrative noise.

tema: Evaluates microstructural abnormalities in ME/CFS using diffusion tensor imaging (DTI).
diseno: Cross-sectional study with DTI in 25 patients (Fukuda criteria), 18 (ICC criteria) and 26 healthy controls; voxel-wise comparisons and interaction regressions with clinical and autonomic measures.
hallazgos: In the ICC group there was lower axial and mean diffusivity in the descending cortico-cerebellar tract of the midbrain and pons, higher transverse diffusivity in the medulla and lower anisotropy mode in the superior longitudinal fasciculus; the Fukuda group showed no differences.
conclusion: DTI is sensitive to microstructural changes in ICC ME/CFS and the brainstem abnormality could be a biomarker; a strict case definition is essential.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent on diffusivity and microstructure; abstract and conclusions reinforce the importance of the ICC criteria, an aspect absent from the keywords.

tema: Systematically evaluates the frequency of viral infections in ME/CFS to investigate their aetiopathogenic role.
diseno: Systematic review and meta-analysis (PubMed and Cochrane up to December 2022): 64 studies on 18 viral species, 4971 ME/CFS patients and 9221 healthy controls or controls with 10 other diseases; odds ratio comparison.
hallazgos: HHV-7, parvovirus B19 (and its co-infection), Borna disease virus (BDV), enterovirus and Coxsackie B virus showed OR > 2.0. BDV exceeded the threshold with OR ≥ 3.47 versus healthy and diseased controls (moderate association).
conclusion: It is the first meta-analysis to systematically examine many relevant viruses; it identifies BDV, parvovirus B19 and Coxsackie B as candidates and provides reference data for future studies, despite its limitations.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the keywords list precisely the viruses highlighted. The PDF conclusions broaden the candidates beyond the BDV that the abstract stresses and acknowledge limitations.

tema: To look for metabolomic evidence of peroxisomal dysfunction in ME/CFS.
diseno: Case-control with 106 patients and 91 controls; targeted and untargeted metabolomics of 888 plasma analytes; regression, Bayesian and enrichment analysis; machine learning.
hallazgos: Reduced plasmalogens, fewer phosphatidylcholines, sphingomyelins, choline, ceramides and carnitines; elevated dicarboxylic acids; maximum AUC of 0.794 in women and 0.873 without self-reported IBS.
conclusion: Interconnected alterations suggest dysfunction of peroxisomes, the CDP-choline cycle and the TCA cycle, consistent with compromised energy metabolism and redox imbalance.
triangulacion: Consistent among the three sources; the conclusions (preprint, with abbreviation noise) link the TCA cycle with physical and cognitive fatigue.

tema: Evaluates whether there is a hereditary predisposition to ME/CFS through familial aggregation analysis.
diseno: Population-based study with a computerized genealogical resource from Utah (UPDB, up to 15 generations) linked to diagnoses from a large health system; comparison of relatedness among cases and relative risk in first- to third-degree relatives. Number of cases not stated.
hallazgos: Relatedness among cases was significantly greater than expected, both close (p < 0.001) and distant (p = 0.010). The relative risk was elevated in first- (2.70), second- (2.34) and third-degree relatives (1.93).
conclusion: The results strongly support a hereditary contribution to the predisposition to ME/CFS; the risks in distant relatives would indicate a genetic component beyond the shared environment.
triangulacion: The three sources agree on familial aggregation and genetic susceptibility. The keywords mention XMRV, which appears only as context in the abstract. The conclusions qualify that first-degree risk is not enough to demonstrate heritability and note as a limitation the narrow diagnostic window.

tema: Evaluates the prevalence of ME/CFS in early limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis and whether a mitochondrial signature distinguishes fatigued from non-fatigued patients.
diseno: Observational study in patients with systemic sclerosis (ACR/EULAR criteria, <5 years of disease); validated questionnaires of ME/CFS symptoms and qPCR of electron transport chain transcripts and mtDNA integrity. Sample size not stated.
hallazgos: Patients with ME/CFS were distinguished from non-fatigued ones by lower expression of ND4 and CyB and higher expression of Cox7C. ND4 and CyB expression correlated with indicators of disease severity.
conclusion: There is a mitochondrial signature specific to ME/CFS in systemic sclerosis, which could be an independent manifestation of the disease linked to a worse prognosis; prospective and functional studies are required.
triangulacion: The three sources agree on the mitochondrial signature (ND4, CyB). The conclusions go somewhat beyond the abstract in asserting a central role of ME/CFS in early morbidity and raising the worse-prognosis hypothesis.

tema: Evaluates, through a systematic review and meta-analysis, whether heart rate parameters reflect altered cardiac autonomic regulation in ME/CFS.
diseno: Systematic review of case-control studies (64 articles included) with meta-analysis of ten categories of heart rate and HRV parameters.
hallazgos: Patients had higher resting heart rate (MD 4.14), tilt-table heart rate (SMD 0.92), orthostatic response (0.50) and resting LF/HF ratio (0.39), and lower maximum heart rate (MD -13.81), anaerobic threshold heart rate (-0.44) and resting HF component (-0.34).
conclusion: ME/CFS patients show altered cardiac autonomic regulation, suggestive of lower vagal and higher sympathetic modulation; no single parameter appears to have sufficient diagnostic sensitivity.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the PDF conclusions are more cautious than the abstract in pointing out high statistical heterogeneity and methodological problems that limit diagnostic usefulness.

tema: Evaluates brain metabolites linked to inflammation and brain temperature in ME/CFS using whole-brain MR spectroscopy.
diseno: Case-control study with whole-brain multivoxel MRS in 15 women with ME/CFS and 15 controls matched for age and sex.
hallazgos: Widely distributed metabolite and brain temperature abnormalities were observed, rather than being limited to specific regions.
conclusion: The results support the hypothesis of chronic low-grade neuroinflammation and diffuse processes throughout the brain; they are preliminary and must be replicated in larger samples.
triangulacion: The abstract is truncated opening text (authors and methods, without results); keywords and conclusions agree on neuroinflammation and metabolites, although the choline/creatine or myo-inositol figures appear only in the keywords.

tema: Explores the clinical similarities between ME/CFS and D-lactic acidosis (D-la) to assess shared mechanisms.
diseno: Systematic review of D-la cases published between 1965 and March 2016 with neurological symptoms and elevated D-lactate (59 episodes), qualitative synthesis against ME/CFS diagnostic criteria and narrative review of mechanisms.
hallazgos: Most neurological alterations of D-la overlap with ME/CFS symptoms, especially motor alterations, more prominent in severe presentations. Both groups share gastrointestinal abnormalities and dysbiosis, although the evidence on lactate-producing bacteria in ME/CFS is preliminary.
conclusion: They propose a continuum between the acute (D-la) and chronic (ME/CFS) presentation related to D-lactate absorption, perhaps relevant only to a subgroup; D-lactate needs to be measured in ME/CFS.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions are consistent on D-lactate, microbiota and the gut-brain axis. The PDF conclusions are more cautious: they acknowledge that no studies have measured D-lactate in ME/CFS and that other mechanisms were outside the scope.

tema: Compares exercise-induced changes in cerebrospinal fluid miRNAs in Gulf War illness (GWI), CFS and sedentary controls.
diseno: Case-control study with lumbar puncture after overnight rest or after submaximal cycling exercise; GWI (START and STOPP phenotypes), CFS and controls (e.g., without exercise: GWI n = 22, CFS n = 43, controls n = 22); miRNA by quantitative PCR.
hallazgos: Without exercise, miRNA levels were equivalent between groups. After exercise, START had less miR-22-3p than controls and STOPP, and more miR-9-3p than STOPP; all post-exercise groups reduced miR-328 and miR-608, and CFS showed 12 decreased miRNAs.
conclusion: Despite the symptom overlap, exercise-induced CSF miRNA patterns indicate distinct mechanisms of PEM in CFS and in the START and STOPP phenotypes of GWI.
triangulacion: The sources are consistent in the essentials; there is an internal discrepancy: the abstract describes miR-328 and miR-608 as reduced after exercise and the PDF conclusions as elevated. The keywords highlight POTS and miR-22-3p.

tema: Analyses whether exercise-induced changes in pain modulation are associated with activation of the complement system (C4a) and elastase in ME/CFS.
diseno: Secondary analysis of controlled experimental studies with 22 ME/CFS patients and 22 sedentary controls; submaximal and self-paced exercise; pressure pain thresholds (PPT) and blood samples.
hallazgos: Elastase was not associated with PPT changes. In ME/CFS, C4a changes were associated with PPT changes after both exercises (r=0.669 at the thumb after submaximal; r=0.429 at the calf after self-paced); C4a predicted PPT change (R2=0.236). No correlations in controls.
conclusion: There are moderate associations between immune changes and pain thresholds only in ME/CFS, suggesting a link between immune alteration and dysfunctional endogenous pain modulation, although with caution.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent. The abstract and discussion stress caution (only one of three PPT measures was associated) and the discussion adds that C4a decreased in both groups.

tema: Investigates the joint potential of inflammatory markers, immunoglobulins and autoantibodies against receptors to assess ME/CFS progression.
diseno: Cross-sectional study in 188 individuals (54 controls; 30 mild, 73 moderate and 31 severe according to Fukuda/CDC 1994 and international consensus criteria); ELISA and multiplex in plasma; correlations, PCA, linear discriminant analysis and random forest.
hallazgos: The association between inflammome and immunome is broader and stronger in the severe group. Random forest reached over 90% accuracy to separate healthy from patients and 45% to distinguish severity levels; the best classifiers were anti-β2AdR, anti-M4, IgG4, IL-2 and IL-6.
conclusion: Inflammation-immunity coupling characterizes the severe group and is a candidate marker of progression in controlled clinical studies; longitudinal observations and longer projects are required.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent on immune markers and severity. The keywords (IFN-γ, TNF-α) do not include the autoantibodies against receptors, which are the most powerful classifiers; the conclusions add the need for longitudinal follow-up and include figure text.

tema: Update on the clinical features, burden and diagnostic criteria of fibromyalgia with a proposed management flow.
diseno: Critical narrative review based on recent literature, EULAR recommendations and clinical experience.
hallazgos: Worldwide prevalence of 2-3%; polysymptomatology with widespread pain, exhaustion, sleep, autonomic and cognitive disturbances; underdiagnosis and the absence of biomarkers persist.
conclusion: Diagnosis remains clinical and subject to the evolution of the criteria; composite tests exist to assess intensity and evolution.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent and centred on fibromyalgia; there is no specific focus on ME/CFS, apart from fatigue as a shared symptom.

tema: Analyses whether fatigue in primary Sjögren's syndrome (pSS) is associated with signs of immunological activity and patient-reported outcomes.
diseno: Letter with cross-sectional study of pSS patients (about 90 according to the table); Spearman correlations with ESSPRI, HAQ, ESR, β2-microglobulin, immunoglobulins and complement.
hallazgos: Fatigue correlated with other patient-reported indices, disease duration and signs of inflammatory activity (serum IgG, β2-microglobulin, ESR). Patients without fatigue had lower IgG (9.81 versus 15.6 g/L) and lower β2-microglobulin.
conclusion: Fatigue reflects the inflammatory activity of pSS, suggesting that acting on inflammation could relieve it and underscoring the need for effective therapies.
triangulacion: The abstract is only the header of the letter with the introduction, and the conclusions come from the discussion with tables; both agree with the keywords on immunological activity and patient-reported outcomes. There is no explicit reference to ME/CFS.

tema: Critically reviews fatigue in ANCA-associated vasculitis and systemic sclerosis (SSc) and its similarities with ME/CFS.
diseno: Critical literature review in MEDLINE, APA PsycInfo, Embase and CINAHL, with screening and extraction by independent researchers; no meta-analysis because of heterogeneity.
hallazgos: Mean fatigue prevalence was 71% in primary vasculitides and 59% in SSc; it was associated with physical function, depression, pain and poor sleep quality, and little or not at all with disease activity or severity. The three conditions share mitochondrial dysregulation, Th2 polarization, low IgG and lower NK cytotoxicity.
conclusion: There are common immune and metabolic pathways; clinicians should identify patients with ME/CFS features, who may require alternative approaches. In these diseases, exercise and behavioural changes could improve fatigue, although these approaches are questioned in ME/CFS.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions are consistent. The PDF conclusions provide prevalence figures, the specific shared mechanisms and limitations (English only, publication bias) that the abstract does not detail.

tema: Analyses faecal metagenomics and plasma immune molecules in ME/CFS, stratifying by comorbidity with irritable bowel syndrome (IBS).
diseno: Case-control study: 50 ME/CFS patients (Fukuda and/or Canadian criteria, Chronic Fatigue Initiative cohort) and 50 matched controls; faecal bacterial metagenomics, topological analysis, predictive models and plasma immune profile.
hallazgos: Comorbidity with IBS was the main factor separating bacterial profiles. In ME/CFS with IBS, the increase in Alistipes and decrease in Faecalibacterium stood out; without IBS, an increase in unclassified Bacteroides and a decrease in Bacteroides vulgatus. Some metabolic pathways (lower unsaturated fatty acid biosynthesis) were independent of IBS and taxa abundance correlated with pain, fatigue and motivation.
conclusion: ME/CFS is associated with dysbiosis and bacterial metabolic alterations independent of IBS, although the high prevalence of IBS may mask features specific to ME/CFS.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions are consistent on dysbiosis and the modulating role of IBS. The conclusions text also includes part of the methods (noise); the plasma immune molecules showed no association, a nuance that the keywords do not reflect.
